subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt or refresh the open fork PR that closes this issue, or create a target-repo replacement for the same source-proven fix?
rationale: The bug and likely fix shape are clear, but there is already an exact open conflicting fork PR plus a partial same-repo PR, so automation should not queue a duplicate until maintainers choose the ownership path.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Focused Fix
options.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement that covers both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

options.title: Wait On Existing Fork PR
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and wait for the contributor to refresh it into a target-repo merge path.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Reminder Work
options.body: Defer this exact bug behind broader reminder-guard cleanup, accepting that the isolated-cron false positive remains open meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Adopt Or Replace Focused Fix
recommendation.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement that covers both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior active-cron suppression and recently touched the current guard/runtime surface, making them the best available routing owner for the adopt-or-replace choice.
